# Motion graphics: flat infographic, kinetic type, product UI film

Graphic films built from a strict system of type, shape and colour, drawn as SVG in Remotion.
- **Flat infographic** (Kurzgesagt-like vector): data, comparisons, processes, science. Geometric
  shapes, a strict palette, charts that build.
- **Kinetic typography:** quotes, manifestos, short punchy lines, sound-off feeds. The words are
  the picture: type moves with its meaning, synced to the voice.
- **Product UI film** (Apple, Linear launches): software launches and feature demos. The real
  interface on a dark stage, headline lines in sequence, smooth ease-in-out with no bounce, and
  outgoing text leaving before incoming arrives.

## Built in code
- Set the system before components: type scale, spacing ramp and palette, each accent with a
  single meaning.
- Draw real interfaces from scratch at true layout (screenshots of the real thing as reference);
  the [phone part](../../templates/parts/README.md) shows a dark-mode iMessage thread.
- Raster art scaled above its native size goes soft. Product photos with opaque backgrounds can't
  be keyed cleanly: get transparent assets or plan around them.

## Its bar
- **Picture first.** Cover the words: if a beat stops reading, redesign the picture instead of
  adding labels. Outside kinetic type, words are for real names, numbers and quotes the picture
  can't carry, each line on screen long enough to read. A large number can be the
  hero of a shot when the narration's point is the number.
- **Concrete over symbolic.** Diegetic UI and real objects (a phone, a message, a to-do list) read
  faster than symbolic shapes.
- **Vary the visual vocabulary from beat to beat.** One motif repeated through a climax read as
  the flattest part of a piece, and a set of scenes built from one page-plus-text vocabulary was
  rejected as unexciting.
- **Carry the central tension through the middle.** Feature sections turn into ads unless the
  story thread is called back.

## Typical failure
Icons in coloured circles and symbols instead of real things; invented UI or a generic glowing
card standing in for the product; kinetic type whose motion makes the words harder to read.
